resolutions.end_name: Ayoun Moussa Steam Power Station (Suez thermal power station complex near the Ahmed Hamdi Tunnel crossing)
resolutions.corridor_desc: GEM's own StartState/EndState 'North Sinia' is directionally consistent with a Sinai-side (east-bank) trunk, but the actual power station polygon (verified via OSM) sits at 29.91N/32.60E near the Ahmed Hamdi Tunnel crossing -- OSM's own reverse-geocode tags that specific spot 'Suez' governorate, and multiple independent tourism/geography sources place the Ayoun Moussa/Ayun Musa toponym in South Sinai (~20-25 km south of the tunnel), not North Sinai. GEM's governorate field for this row may be wrong on both ends (flagged, not corrected). The EIB's 1998 press release for GASCO's financing of 'two gas pipelines, one on each bank of the Suez Canal ... to carry natural gas from Egypt's offshore fields in the Mediterranean Sea to the Ayoun Moussa Power Station in the Sinai' establishes the general feed concept (Mediterranean-sourced gas via a west-bank + Sinai-bank pipeline pair) but describes a 275 km EIB-financed project -- likely a distinct or predecessor project to this 145 km/24in line, not a confirmed match. No source found ties a specific named northern origin point to THIS 145 km pipeline; a WebSearch AI summary that claimed a GASCO trunk 'passing by Oyoun Mousa, El-Arish & Rafah ending in Sharm El-Sheikh' could NOT be confirmed against the archived source text (the actual article at theenergyyear.com only says the grid 'is extending east to Sinai ... and along the coast of the Red Sea', a much vaguer statement) -- that specific claim is discarded as unverifiable, per the hard rule against fabrication.
